newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares held onto most of their early strong gains to close at yet another fresh record on Thursday, bouyed by rises across Europe and Wall Street's hefty near 100-point rally overnight.
The AEX index of Dutch blue chip stocks ended 9.44 points, or 1.25 percent, higher at 764.67, a new record. The index also touched a new intra-day record peak of 765.89.
Strong backgroud factors were boosted by a heavy corporate results day, with three major companies reporting uear figures.
"The market still feels pretty strong and with the results today there was a lot of interest," one dealer said.
The day kicked off with full-year earnings for steel and aluminium maker Hoogovens, which reported pre-bourse sharply lower profits but well above market expectations.

The group said 1996 net was 326 million guilders, against 504 million in 1995 but the figure was above the range forecast by analysts of between 260 and 310 million. Dealers said buying in the stock was also spurred by an optimisitc outlook for 1997.

Hoogovens said it expected "the net results from ordinary operations will improve during the course of 1997" as moderate economic growth in Europe had a positive impact on demand for steel and aluminium products.
Hoogovens shares jumped sharply at the opening, reaching a high at 98.00 guilders but then eased back to end at 92.60, up 1.60 guilders on the day.

Drinks and food group BolsWessanen was the next company to issue earnings figures. It reported net profit from normal ops down 9.2 percent, slightly better than its own forecast of a 10 percent fall, and predicted a 1997 operating improvement.
The food and drink group's net from normal operations in 1996 fell to 184.2 million guilders from 202.9 million while turnover crept up to 4.69 billion guilders from 4.63 billion.
Analysts had anticipated a figure of around 181 million.
The shares were strong ahead of the results but lost a little of their shine afterwards, ending 1.30 higher at 36.20.
"I think people were expecting a little too much," one dealer said, adding the results were basically sound.

In the afternoon retailer Ahold announced its 1996 earnings, with net profits surging 39 percent to 632.4 million guilders from 456.6 million a year earlier. It also said it would split its shares on a three-for-one basis.
The market reacted favourably and the shares shot to a high of 139.00 guilders before easing back to end 5.20 up at 137.40.
